title: Return NA from get_maintainer() when Authors@R cannot be parsed
description:
`$get_maintainer()` formatted the result of `$get_author("cre")` unconditionally. When `Authors@R` cannot be parsed, that result is `NULL`, and `format(NULL)` gave the string `"NULL"`.

It now returns `NA_character_` in that case, the same value the method already returns when there is neither a `Maintainer` nor an `Authors@R` field. Results for valid `Authors@R` (with or without a `cre`), a `Maintainer` field, and a missing field are unchanged.

Closes #140

title: Implement tidy-on-write feature
description:
This pull request introduces the tidy-on-write functionality controlled by the `Config/desc/tidy` setting. It adds a configuration check to automatically tidy package DESCRIPTION files when the setting is enabled, provides supporting helper methods (`get_config`, `get_config_value`), updates the description class, and includes tests and documentation improvements. The change also removes the now-unnecessary `desc_add_ror` function and makes documentation updates.

Fixes #133

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to desc website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the desc website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

My main assumptions underlying the code:

title: Implements write() for DESCRIPTION files backed by package archives
description:
This PR implements `write()` functionality for `DESCRIPTION` files backed by package archives, which would be useful for a project of mine. I'm not totally sure why this was not implemented before, so forgive me if there is a principled reason to forbid it.

The approach is basically

* For zip archives, we can use the replace functionality in `zip()` to update the `DESCRIPTION` file in-place.

* For tar archives, we must (1) extract the package contents, (2) modify the `DESCRIPTION` file, and then (3) re-archive the result in the same fashion as `R CMD build`, since tar archives do not support in-place modification.

In addition, this PR updates the docs to remove the restriction and removes the test that an error would occur if a user tried to call the `write()` method.

Known issues:

* The tar archive may not preserve file order and does not preserve modification times on directory entries. I don't think either of these is a dealbreaker.

In addition, I have not tested this on Windows.

title: multiple roles can be applied to each person
description:
In the original implementation, multiple roles cannot be applied to role argument for functions such as desc$add_author(). This is because check_author_args() function called from add_author() calls is_string_or_null() for role argument. This checks whether the role is NULL or character vector with length of 1.
In the develop implementation for that I am creating pull request, role argument can be character vector with any length. Instead of is_string_or_null(), is_character_or_null() is implemented and used. 

The following code is allowed in this implementation.
```
desc$add_author("Bugs", "Bunny", email = "bb@example.com", role=c("ctb", "cph"))
```

title: Fix text inputs with marked encodings
description:
If `desc()` was called with a text parameter and the input was _not_ in
the default encoding for the locale `textConnection()` would be called
with the default encoding parameter of `""`, which attempts to convert
the encoding to the default one. Using encoding = "bytes" means the
connection does not try to convert the encoding and just passes the
bytes through unchanged, which fixes the issue.
